text:
john: FYI PulseGrid support ticket — p95 jumped from ~600ms to ~2s after the 12:03 deploy. Customer seeing timeouts. link: https://grafana.redwood/pulsegrid/request-p95 :eyes:
deploy-bot: deploy finished by kevin at 2023-11-29T12:03:02Z - sha abc123
kevin: taking a look now. rolling logs for that timeframe show a surge in queue depth in routing-service.
miguel: can you paste the routing logs / queue metrics? any change in batch config or new model variant released?
john: logs clipped: `routing.queue_depth=230`, `worker.wait_ms=1200`, `model.variant=redwood-v2-q4`
sara: interesting — we pushed an autoscaler tweak earlier that increases max-batch-size from 64->128 for some pools. that could amplify queueing for short requests.
kevin: confirmed autoscaler tweak merged in runtime-config at 11:58. rolling back that commit for the affected pool now.
sara: +1 to rollback if we see immediate impact. i wonder if the prefix cache missed after deploy causing more full-token compute.
kevin: rollback started — will report back when done.
miguel: miguel here — triggering oncall runbook. asking for traces: can we get a sample trace id for a slow request?
john: sample trace: trace-id=tr_0x9f8a, attached slow span: `model.generate` with 1.9s dominator.
sara: span shows repeated `wait_for_batch` stalls. batch scheduler waiting 250-300ms repeatedly. that aligns with larger max-batch-size causing backlog.
ellie: product context — how many customers affected & revenue impact? PulseGrid says their throughput dropped and they hit 5xxs for key customers. need severity assessment for roadmap/prioritization.
john: pulsegrid support says ~7% of requests 5xx for last 20m, paying tier, flagged as P1 by AM.
ellie: ok thx. decision needed: rollback config (short-term) + follow-up to change rollout gating and add canary for batching change.
sara: agree. short-term rollback in progress. long-term: add a canary that prevents max-batch-size increases from applying to low-latency customer pools without verification.
kevin: rollback completed at 12:12 — metrics starting to trend back down. p95 back to ~650ms.
john: PulseGrid confirms degraded requests dropping, says they see improvement. :thumbsup:
miguel: leaving note in oncall: `incident: routing-queueing-2030456789`, linking grafana/dumps.
ellie: product actions: 1) create a customer-intake ticket and add to backlog 2) define launch criteria for batching/autoscaler changes (safety net + perf A/B) 3) prioritize a quick eval of per-customer rollout flags.
sara: tech actions: create RT ticket RT-2983: "Canary + gating for batching/autoscaler changes"; instrument batch scheduler with request-tagged tracing; add alert for queue_depth>100 for 5m.
kevin: i'll own the RT ticket and put a small PR up for the canary in runtime tomorrow. estimate: 2 days to prototype, 1 sprint to fully QA and roll out.
ellie: product will allocate a chunk of upcoming ops-planning sprint to support QA and write launch criteria. we'll flag this as customer-driven priority.
miguel: oncall closing thread but keep monitoring for 1h. if regression returns we may re-open escalation.
john: adding note to PulseGrid ticket that we've rolled back and created RT-2983; asking for monitoring window and offer to schedule a postmortem if needed.
sara: postmortem/notes: suspected root cause = un-gated batching increase interacting with short-request workload -> queueing stalls at scheduler -> p95 spike. mitigation = rollback + canary + telemetry.
ellie: assigning outcomes: backlog: RT-2983 (owner kevin), Postmortem doc (owner sara), Customer comms (owner john). target: ship canary + alerting before next autoscaler config change. :white_check_mark:
kevin: noted. I'll attach a replay of the batch scheduler traces to RT-2983.
miguel: closing — monitoring window still open. ping here if PulseGrid reports recurrence.
john: PulseGrid says they're back to nominal. closing support loop pending postmortem. thanks team.
